clue.text: "Golden Lives", period 11 in film

definitions.note: the star who played the title role of 11-down in the 1953 film

parts.note: d'or is French for 'of gold', as in Palme d'Or, so golden
lives means exists, is
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A film title or tagline about golden lives, with a time period from a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' points to the musical at 11-down; the actress who played its heroine on screen is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The American actress and singer took the lead role in the 1953 Hollywood musical, so she is the screen heroine.

clue.text: A point inside of French flower

indicators.note: inside places the article and point within the French word

parts.note: de is French for 'of'
a nub is a small point or knob, the crux

explanation.surface: A small point found inside some French bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword's thing that flows, a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a flow-er in crossword terms, and this is the great European river through Vienna and Budapest.

clue.text: Heartless fugitive on airfield

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: a fugitive is a runaway

explanation.surface: A cruel escaped convict is found on an airfield.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is the strip on an airfield where planes take off and land, standing for the airfield itself.

clue.text: Set off publicity which leads to firing

parts.note: to spark is to set off or trigger
a plug is a piece of publicity for a product

explanation.surface: Triggering a publicity campaign that ends with someone being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firing' suggests dismissal from a job; here it is the ignition of fuel in an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: This engine component makes the spark that ignites the fuel, so it leads to the cylinder firing.

clue.text: Piece of 11 coming from lady's fingers

definitions.meaning: a song from the musical at 11-down
the touch of a female hand, literally from a lady's fingers

explanation.definitionFit: It is a song in the musical, and also the phrase for a deft feminine touch, made by a woman's hand.

clue.text: Finn on board? Oh dear! It's American

indicators.note: being on board a ship means sitting within the abbreviation for steamship

parts.note: the ship one is on board, SS for steamship
Huck Finn, Mark Twain's boy hero

explanation.surface: Asking whether Twain's boy hero is aboard ship, and sighing about something American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the convention for placing something between S and S (steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: It is an American exclamation of mild dismay or embarrassment, much like saying oh dear.

clue.text: See 12
Vegetable cover (that's right? I'm not sure)

parts.note: a cap is a cover, as on a bottle
sic is written in a quotation to confirm it is exactly right as given
um is a hesitant noise of uncertainty

explanation.surface: A vegetable lid, with the speaker doubting whether that's correct.
explanation.walkthrough: SIC, Latin 'thus', is the editor's note meaning the quoted text is correct as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: The pepper plant and its fruit, eaten as a vegetable, bear this botanical name.

clue.text: Very angry look at article

parts.note: to see is to look at
an article is an object, a thing

explanation.surface: Someone furious glaring at an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' tempts as A, AN or THE; here it is an object.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to boil with suppressed rage, so seething means furious, very angry.

clue.text: Coventry is at hand: don't interrupt your meal, sister

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
to eat on is to keep eating without a break

explanation.surface: A nun told to keep eating, with the city of Coventry nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: This Warwickshire market town lies just north of Coventry, so from it that city is close at hand.

clue.text: Fall asleep?

indicators.note: letters falling into a new order, so the following word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A simple question about dozing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' looks like part of the phrase 'fall asleep' but rearranges the letters of 'asleep'.
explanation.definitionFit: When you drop off to sleep, time slips by unnoticed, passing while you are unconscious.

clue.text: Musical friendship with German consent in Wiltshire town

indicators.note: in places the friendship and consent inside the town name

parts.note: Calne is a market town in Wiltshire, an English county
amity is friendship
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A stage show about German agreement and goodwill set in a West Country town.
explanation.walkthrough: CALNE is a small town in Wiltshire, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1953 Hollywood musical starring a famous blonde singer is named after its Wild West heroine.

clue.text: Deficiency in Broad-casting House leads to troubles in 26

indicators.note: in places the shortage between the two leading letters
leads gives the first letters of the two words

parts.note: a lack is a deficiency
ills are troubles

explanation.surface: A shortage at the BBC's London headquarters causes problems out in the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcasting House is the BBC's London home; the hyphen just separates the word. '26' is the US state region at 26-across, where these mountains lie.
explanation.definitionFit: This mountain range lies in the territory of 26-across, the setting of a song in the musical.

clue.text: A mother struck hard by an economist

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
smit is an old past tense of smite, struck
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A mother hit hard by some economist.
explanation.walkthrough: SMIT is an archaic form of 'smote' or 'smitten', meaning struck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish thinker who wrote The Wealth of Nations is the founding figure of modern economics.

clue.text: Oblique effect of UN brand to produce bare soil

parts.note: an oblique is a slash, the punctuation stroke

indicators.note: the effect of something reworks the letters of the words given

explanation.surface: The roundabout influence of a United Nations label on stripping land bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'effect of' rearranges UN BRAND into ANDBURN.
explanation.definitionFit: This farming practice cuts and burns vegetation to clear land, leaving bare soil for cultivation.

clue.text: A number of warmers on a bike for police department

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
rugs keep you warm
a quad is a quad bike, a four-wheeled motorbike

explanation.surface: Several blankets loaded onto a motorbike for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the specialist police unit dealing with narcotics offences, so a department of the force.

clue.text: Ruined 22 due to having dropped eggs

indicators.note: ruined means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: the answer to 22-down, a green tweed shade

explanation.surface: A green cloth spoiled because a hen laid her eggs on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' scrambles LOVAT (22-down) with DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ovulate is to release an egg from the ovary, so this means having released eggs.

clue.text: Mouse's leader is a sort of beetle — that's its problem

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the click beetle snaps itself upright with a clicking sound

explanation.surface: A small rodent leading a kind of insect, which is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'mouse' is the computer kind, whose trouble is a wrong press of a button.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer mouse's trouble is an accidental button press, the wrong selection on screen.

clue.text: Log in, perhaps, inter-rupting divers given to bragging

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the word for divers

parts.note: divers is an old word for various, several

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters may be in another order

explanation.surface: Computer users logging in and bothering underwater swimmers who like to boast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' here is the old adjective meaning several, not swimmers. 'perhaps' rearranges LOG IN into INGLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Vainglory is boastful pride, so someone vainglorious brags excessively.

clue.text: Begin to cheat with grass to make curtain

indicators.note: begin to means only the opening part of the synonym is kept

parts.note: to bamboozle is to cheat or hoodwink

explanation.surface: Starting to swindle with grass to make a hanging screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bamboo Curtain was the political barrier around communist Asia, after the Iron Curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tall woody grass, and the phrase Bamboo Curtain named the barrier around communist China.

clue.text: Top man in glass ball

indicators.note: in places the man inside the glass ball

parts.note: a bead is a small glass ball
he is a man's pronoun

explanation.surface: A leading man inside a crystal ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a noun; it is the verb meaning to cut the head off.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is slang for executing them, and beheading is one way of doing it.

clue.text: Water or waters — your first — in the Great Glen

parts.note: a loch is a Scottish lake, a body of water
a loch is again a stretch of waters

indicators.note: first gives the opening letter of the word your

explanation.surface: Choosing between one lake or several, with you going first, somewhere in a Scottish valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Glen is the long valley across the Scottish Highlands holding Loch Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: This freshwater lake lies along the Great Glen, between Loch Oich and Fort William.

clue.text: Green tax — see over it

indicators.note: over means the look word sits above the tax in this down clue

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, see
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: An environmental tax, with a note to read the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' tempts as eco-friendly; it is a colour. VAT is the UK sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a muted grey-green colour, typical of Scottish tweeds.

clue.text: See 27
Rob hit out at First Lady

indicators.note: out signals the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A man named Rob lashing out at the President's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob' looks like a name; it is the verb to steal. 'out' rearranges HIT into THI.
explanation.definitionFit: To rob someone is to steal from them, the act of a thief.

clue.text: Loo backed with a blue mixture that could fetch a bit

indicators.note: backed means the word for loo is read backwards

parts.note: lav, short for lavatory, is a loo

indicators.note: a mixture blends the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A toilet with a blue mix that might sell for a decent sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns LAV into VAL; 'mixture' rearranges A BLUE into UABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth a lot of money would fetch a good price at sale.

clue.text: Aircraft of North and South?

definitions.meaning: the Douglas transport plane of the Second World War
the American states of that name come as a North and a South pair

explanation.definitionFit: It is the RAF name for the Douglas C-47 plane and the name shared by two US states.

clue.text: Piece of 11, useless stuff at theatre

parts.note: deadwood is useless people or material
the stage stands for the theatre profession

explanation.surface: Redundant junk lying around a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of 11' is a song from the musical at 11-down.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the opening song of the musical, named for the stagecoach to the Dakota frontier town.
